context: Linked parallel coordinates + world map explorer for 40 cities across 6 dimensions (population, density, elevation, temp, rainfall, cost index), with brush-to-filter on axes and hover tooltips.
first_impression: Clean and restrained — the monochromatic blue-on-dark theme and just two linked views keep cognitive load low, though the parallel coordinates show moderate line tangling.
what_works: Single-hue color scheme entirely avoids color overload; the two views are conceptually complementary (filter by attributes in parcoords, see geographic distribution on map) and the alpha-layering (faint ghost lines vs. bright selected lines) makes the selection state immediately legible.
what_doesnt: The Elevation axis creates a visual bottleneck where the majority of cities cluster near 0 m, causing heavy line convergence that makes individual traces untrackable in that region; the map dots are uniform in size and color regardless of selection state at rest, so the map adds geographic context but no additional data encoding — a missed pairing with the parcoords dimensions.
